title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Economics (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Economics (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: What is the payback period of the project having a constant cash flow of birr 5000 each year over its 10 year's life time span if the initial investment outlay is birr 35000?
options: 5 years and 3 months
8 years
7 years
4 years and 3 months
questions.explanation: The payback period is calculated by dividing the initial investment by the annual cash flow: 35000/5000 = 7 years.

questions.questionText: The underlying assumption of the Harrod - Domar growth model is that:
options: The incremental capital - output ratio is given by k = Y/K.
Growth is mainly determined by capital accumulation.
Growth can be sustained only if productivity rises.
Developing countries save too much and invest too little.
questions.explanation: The Harrod-Domar model emphasizes the role of capital accumulation in driving economic growth.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a dummy variable?
options: Employment Status
Sex
Distance
Poverty Status
questions.explanation: Distance is a continuous variable, while the others are categorical.

questions.questionText: If we do not reject the null hypothesis, we conclude that:
options: There is enough statistical evidence to infer that the alternative hypothesis is true.
There is not enough statistical evidence to infer that the alternative hypothesis is true.
There is enough statistical evidence to infer that the null hypothesis is true.
The test is statistically insignificant at whatever level of significance.
questions.explanation: Not rejecting the null hypothesis indicates insufficient evidence against it.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a main factor for the low-productivity subsistence farming characteristic of most traditional African agriculture:
options: Only small areas can be planted and weeded by the farm family
Usage of traditional farming tools
Given the limited amount of land, productivity is subject to rapidly diminishing returns with increase in number of population
Labor is unemployed or underemployed during peak production season
questions.explanation: During peak production season, labor is typically fully employed in traditional farming. Unemployment or underemployment is more common during slack seasons, not peak seasons.

questions.questionText: Liquidity of an asset will increase with the following factors. Except:
options: The more its price is stable
The more it is indivisible
The lower the transaction cost to buy the asset
The easier it can be converted into cash.
questions.explanation: Indivisibility typically reduces liquidity, as it cannot be easily divided for sale.

questions.questionText: An optimal strategy of player no matter the strategy chosen by other player is called:
options: Mixed strategy
Pure strategy
Dominant strategy
Nash Equilibrium
questions.explanation: A dominant strategy is optimal regardless of the opponent's actions.

questions.questionText: Suppose the average product of 6 workers is 150 units of a good and that of 7 workers is 170 units. The MP of the seventh worker equals:
questions.explanation: Marginal Product (MP) of the 7th worker is calculated as the change in total output from adding one more worker. Total output with 6 workers = 6 × 150 = 900. Total output with 7 workers = 7 × 170 = 1190. Therefore, MP = 1190 - 900 = 290.

questions.questionText: If the game is repeated for infinite numbers of time, then which one is not true?
options: Players have opportunity to establish cooperation
Tit-for-tat strategy is considered by players
The equilibrium of the game is similar to one shot game
There is high probability for players to get pareto efficient outcome.
questions.explanation: In repeated games, strategies can evolve differently than in one-shot games.

questions.questionText: Given two commodities X and Y and level of income M, then if the price of the commodity X changes which of the following is true?
options: The budget line shifts to the right.
The budget line shifts to the left.
The slope of the budget line changes.
The X and Y intercept changes together.
questions.explanation: A change in the price of X affects the slope of the budget line.

questions.questionText: One of the following can be a micro level source of project idea:
options: National policies and strategies
Sectoral, sub-sectoral or regional plans
The necessity to complement or expand businesses previously undertaken
Unusual events such as droughts, floods, earthquakes and etc.
questions.explanation: Micro-level sources often stem from the need to expand existing businesses.

questions.questionText: One is not a basic characteristic of a project:
options: project sees many changes throughout its life.
Project having identical or duplicated plants are exactly similar.
There is a concept of unity in diversity in any project.
Projects funded by huge international financial agents are free from risks and uncertainty.
questions.explanation: Identical projects can still differ in many aspects, including context and execution.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among core requirements for agricultural transformation:
options: Improving the overall social, commercial, and institutional conditions under which the farmer is functioning
Providing the Necessary Economic Incentives and opportunities like reasonable and reliable access to credit, fertilizer, water, crop information, and marketing facilities
Price policy in favor of agricultural product in comparing with manufactured good
Making land reform like making fair distribution land from large land holders and government enterprises to either small holders or non-holders farmers
questions.explanation: Price policy is important but not a core requirement for transformation.

questions.questionText: Suppose NGO whose name is Merlin provides a project to pastoralist area. The project resulted in improved variety resistant to diseases, erosion and protecting livestock disease breakout. Such type of the project's benefit/cost is categorized under:
options: Intangible cost
Intangible benefit
Tangible cost
Tangible benefit
questions.explanation: The benefits from improved varieties are tangible as they directly affect productivity.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the characteristic of perfectly competitive market?
options: Many firms each supplying a small fraction of the market
Each firm determines price for its product
Perfectly elastic demand curve for each individual firm
Free flow of information among different economic agents
questions.explanation: In perfect competition, firms are price takers, not price makers.

questions.questionText: In which type of farming the more emphasis is on land and labor productivity instead of capital formation, technological progress, and scientific research and development?
options: Subsistence farming
Mixed farming
Specialized farming
and B
questions.explanation: Subsistence farming focuses on maximizing output with limited resources.

questions.questionText: Total exports as a share of GDP is most probably to be the highest for one of the following regions of the world.
options: Sub Saharan Africa
Europe
East Asia
North America
questions.explanation: East Asia has a high export-oriented economy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the effect of the cut in government expenditure in an alternative AS-AD model in Keynesian supply case?
options: It will result in lower price without affecting real variable such as output and employment.
It will result in outward shift in aggregate demand curve forming new equilibrium at higher level of output without affecting price.
It will result in lower aggregate demand and lower income without affecting price of both inputs and outputs.
It will result in higher price level which in turn reduces the real money balance and leads to increase in interest rate.
questions.explanation: A cut in government spending typically reduces aggregate demand.

questions.questionText: With total approach, when does the point of maximum profit is attained for competitive firm?
options: When both TR and TC reaches maximum
When the difference between TR and TC is zero
When the difference between MR and MC is positive
When positive difference between total revenue and total cost gets maximum
questions.explanation: Maximum profit occurs when the difference between total revenue and total cost is maximized.

questions.questionText: Identify false statement about external trade sector of developing countries.
options: Their export items are generally primary and agricultural output commodities
The real or social opportunity costs of a unit of imports will rise
Developing country's income elasticity demand toward importable items like machineries and technologies is generally low.
Policies designed to reduce severe budget deficit eventually results in lack of effective demand and other macroeconomic imbalance in their economy
questions.explanation: Developing countries typically have high income elasticity of demand for imports, especially for machinery and technology, meaning they spend proportionally more on imports as income rises.

questions.questionText: Change in one of the following factors directly affects the volume of export of a particular nation except _____
options: Price competitiveness of domestic product in international market
Domestic price
Foreigner's price
Exchange rate
questions.explanation: Foreigner's price level does affect export volume through relative price competitiveness. The correct exception would be a different factor not listed among these options.

questions.questionText: One of the following is wrong statement about investment and interest rate.
options: Lower interest rate the more firm will be willing to undertake any given investment project.
The higher interest rate, the higher firm will be willing to participate investment project.
The higher interest rate the less firm will be willing to undertake investment project.
None.
questions.explanation: Higher interest rates typically discourage investment.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not true about perfectly competitive market.
options: Products are not standardized.
The slope of total revenue equals with marginal revenue.
At the ruling market price a firm can sell an infinite number of products.
The demand curve that an individual firm faces is infinitely elastic.
questions.explanation: In a perfectly competitive market, products are standardized.

questions.questionText: Why aggregate demand is inversely related to aggregate price level through operation of money market?
options: quantity theory of money states that increment in price makes each transaction to require more money
The decline in price results in the rise in demand for the real money balance and then rise in aggregate demand
The rise in price results in the rise in the real purchasing power of money and the rise in aggregate demand
and B
questions.explanation: Lower prices increase the real money balance, leading to higher aggregate demand.

questions.questionText: Which of the following trade cooperation can be considered as South-South trade cooperation?
options: Ethiopia Vs. Kenya
Zambia Vs. Zimbabwe
South Korea vs. South Sudan.
All
questions.explanation: South-South trade cooperation involves trade between developing countries.

questions.questionText: One is not a reason for emergence of time value of money.
options: Uncertainty about the future
Expectation about betterment of life in the future
The possibility of making investment with the current sum of money
None
questions.explanation: All listed options are reasons for the time value of money.

questions.questionText: If expected return from the bond is rise, then which one is true?
options: People will shift from the most liquid asset holding to the least liquid asset holding.
People shift from money holding to bond holding.
People will shift from the least liquid asset holding to the most liquid asset holding.
People will choose to hold more money instead of bond.
questions.explanation: Higher expected returns on bonds make them more attractive than holding cash.

questions.questionText: The indifference curve of tea and sugar is more probably:
options: Perfect substitutes with MRS constant.
Perfect complements with MRS zero.
Perfect complements with MRS constant.
Vertical line with no MRS.
questions.explanation: Tea and sugar are typically complementary goods with zero marginal rate of substitution when consumed in fixed proportions.

questions.questionText: A Perfectly competitive firm:
options: Will always sell at the prevailing price
Should reduce its output in order to maximize profit.
May charge below market price to attract more customers.
May charge above market price to show that its product is superior.
questions.explanation: Perfectly competitive firms are price takers and sell at the market price.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the characteristic of perfectly competitive market?
options: Many firms each supplying a small fraction of the market
Each firm determines price for its product
Perfectly elastic demand curve for each individual firm
Free flow of information among different economic agents
questions.explanation: In perfect competition, firms cannot set prices; they are determined by the market.

questions.questionText: The Head Count Ratio of income poverty refers to:
options: The number of people below the poverty line
The proportion of people below the poverty line
The number of adults below the poverty line
The proportion of adults below the poverty line
questions.explanation: The Head Count Ratio measures the proportion of the population living below the poverty line.

questions.questionText: The price used in Economic analysis of a project is called:
options: Shadow price
Market price
Relative price
All except 'A'
questions.explanation: In economic analysis of projects, shadow prices are used to reflect the true opportunity cost when market prices are distorted.

questions.questionText: Consider an economy operating in Keynesian cross model setup with closed economy case. Suppose the economy's basic components are estimated and given as follows. C=200+0.75Yd, I=100, G=350 and T=100. Where, Yd=Y - T. Then one of the following is incorrect:
options: Autonomous aggregate spending and MPC are 575 and 0.75 respectively
Equilibrium national income and consumption are 2300 and 1850
decline in tax rate by 5 more unit, results in decline of national income to 2285 which is shown by entire downward shift of planned expenditure curve
An increase in government expenditure by 10 more $ unit results in the increase of national income to 2340 which is shown by entire upward shift of planned expenditure curve.
questions.explanation: A decline in tax rate increases disposable income, which increases consumption and aggregate demand, leading to higher national income. The statement incorrectly suggests it would decrease national income.

questions.questionText: Trade argument which states that 'Developing nations have their 'static' comparative advantage in primary products, which means that export-promoting free-trade policies tend to inhibit industrialization,' can be consistent with:
options: Trade optimistic view
Inward-looking development policies view
Trade pessimistic view
All except 'A'
questions.explanation: This argument aligns with trade pessimistic view and inward-looking development policies, focusing on the limitations of primary product dependence.

questions.questionText: Which of the following models is used to regress on dummy dependent variable?
options: The LPM model.
The tobit model.
The logit model.
All of the above
questions.explanation: LPM and logit/probit models are used for dummy dependent variables, while the Tobit model is primarily for censored dependent variables.

questions.questionText: Suppose a firm faces the production function Q= 12K^0.4 L^0.4 and assume it can purchase K and L at prices per unit of 40 birr and 5 Birr respectively and it has a budget of 800 Birr. The amount of K and L which maximizes output is:
questions.explanation: With equal exponents (0.4) for K and L in the production function, the optimal allocation occurs when spending on each input is proportional to its exponent. Since both have the same exponent, K and L should have equal budget shares: 40K = 5L, and 40K + 5L = 800. Solving these equations gives K = 10 and L = 80, which corresponds to option A (10, 80).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following options is not true about the various stages of agricultural development?
options: The Law of Diminishing returns of labor is in operation when the farmers' exclusive goal is to supply the output for the market.
Mixed farming can minimize the impact of staple crop failure.
The exclusive emphasis on one particular type of crop is a feature of agriculture commonly practiced by most farmers in developed countries.
Specialized farming is not different in concept or operations from large industrial enterprises.
questions.explanation: Specialized farming often differs significantly from industrial operations.

questions.questionText: According to Harrod - Domar growth model growth is:
options: Directly related to savings and inversely related to the capital/output ratio.
Directly related to the capital/output ratio and inversely related to savings.
Inversely related to savings and the capital/output ratio.
Directly related to savings and the capital/output ratio.
questions.explanation: In the Harrod-Domar model, the growth rate (g) equals the savings rate (s) divided by the capital-output ratio (k): g = s/k. Thus, growth is directly related to savings and inversely related to the capital-output ratio.

questions.questionText: Which one is the most liquid that can be used directly as a medium of exchange?
options: M3
M2
M1
M4
questions.explanation: M1 includes the most liquid forms of money, such as cash and checking deposits.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a tangible cost of the project:
options: Remuneration made to human labor and technical experts involved in the project
Increased pollution as a result of the project
Cost for imported as well as indigenous machineries used for installation of the project.
Costs of identifying the project, conducting the market survey and preparing the feasibility study
questions.explanation: Increased pollution is typically considered an intangible cost.

questions.questionText: Suppose that the technology that is used to produce product X is changed. As a result, employees who are producing X no more fit to the new technology and become unemployed. Such type of unemployment is:
options: Frictional unemployment
Cyclic unemployment
Structural unemployment
Seasonal unemployment
questions.explanation: Structural unemployment occurs when workers' skills do not match the new technology.

questions.questionText: If in regression model, one of the explanatory variables included is the lagged value of the dependent variable, then the model is referred to as:
options: Best fit model
Dynamic model
Autoregressive model
First-difference form
questions.explanation: A model with lagged dependent variables is called an autoregressive model.

questions.questionText: If a Durbin Watson statistic takes a value close to zero, what will be the value of the first order autocorrelation coefficient?
options: Close to zero
Close to plus one
Close to minus one
Close to either minus one or plus one
questions.explanation: A Durbin-Watson statistic close to zero indicates strong positive autocorrelation, with a first-order autocorrelation coefficient close to +1.

questions.questionText: One of the following macroeconomic problems cannot be related to mismanagement of monetary sector:
options: Decline in investment
Unemployment
Inflation
None
questions.explanation: All listed options can be related to mismanagement of the monetary sector.

questions.questionText: From the following test of heteroskedasticity which one is used for large samples & at least sample size is twice the number of explanatory variables.
options: The Breusch - Pagan Test
White's General Heteroskedasticity Test
Goldfeld - Quandt Test
The Spearman rank - correlation Test
questions.explanation: The Breusch-Pagan test is suitable for large samples.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is consistent with Hirschman's theory of unbalanced growth?
options: country should focus on industry, because agriculture is not a dynamic sector.
To initiate the industrialization process a country requires a 'big push.'
When certain industries are developed first, linkage effects will induce the development of new industries.
All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hirschman's theory of unbalanced growth emphasizes that strategic development of certain industries creates linkage effects that induce development in other sectors.

questions.questionText: One of the following agricultural technologies is scale-neutral, which can be equally applied and increases yield per hectare of both small and large farm:
options: Hybrid or improved seeds
New innovation in chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides
New innovation in veterinary medicine and animal nutrition.
All
questions.explanation: All listed technologies can benefit farms of different sizes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following policy measures could be used to solve the problem of frictional unemployment?
options: Increase unemployment benefit
Expand aggregate demand among employees.
Provides better job information.
Increase the level of money supply
questions.explanation: Better job information helps reduce frictional unemployment by matching workers with jobs.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a responsibility of the central bank:
options: It enables the government to issue public debt
It dictates the commercial banks not to invest in risky assets
It acts as a financial and economic adviser to the government
None
questions.explanation: Central banks do not typically dictate specific investment decisions to commercial banks.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not an indicator of development?
options: Living standards
Literacy rate, life expectancy and per capita income
Health, housing, education and nutritional changes
GDP growth only
questions.explanation: GDP growth alone does not provide a comprehensive measure of development.

questions.questionText: Suppose the utility function of the consumer is given by U = 4xy - y^2 and the budget constraint is 2x+y = 6. The amount of x and y which will optimize total utility of the consumer is:
questions.explanation: To maximize U = 4xy - y² subject to 2x + y = 6, use Lagrangian method. The first-order conditions give: 4y = 2λ and 4x - 2y = λ. Solving with the budget constraint yields x = 2, y = 2.

questions.questionText: The supply curve of labor to industry in the Lewis model is horizontal if there is surplus labor in agriculture. This condition persists as long as:
options: The marginal product of labor is less than the average product of labor in agriculture.
The marginal product of labor in agriculture is less than the marginal product of labor in industry.
There are diminishing returns to labor in agriculture.
The marginal product of labor in agriculture is zero.
questions.explanation: Surplus labor means that additional labor does not increase output in agriculture.

questions.questionText: The functional distribution of income refers to the distribution of income between:
options: Individuals or households.
The factors of production.
Rural individuals or households.
Urban individuals or households.
questions.explanation: Functional distribution of income focuses on how income is distributed among factors of production.

questions.questionText: One of the following can't be true about globalization and its effects:
options: Globalization results in single or similar global culture in which different peoples of the world lead similar lifestyle, use similar language and follow similar wearing style.
It is a process in which the whole world is to be governed by single leader/ruler of big nation like America.
Globalization is a process which results in ever increasing economic integration of different nations where different nations of the world pursue similar global economic policy.
In globalization rule only those who are able to compete and win can sustain in the market.
questions.explanation: Globalization does not imply governance by a single leader.

questions.questionText: In which one of the following conditions does the Todaro Model of Migration say a lower rate of rural to urban migration would occur?
options: When there are high economic opportunities in urban areas
When there is high unemployment rate in urban areas, Ceteris Paribas.
When there is high expected urban-rural real wage differential
When there is high actual urban-rural real wage differential
questions.explanation: High unemployment in urban areas discourages migration.

questions.questionText: From the following one is not a test for heteroskedasticity?
options: The Breusch - Pagan Test
Goldfeld - Quandt Test
The Durbin - Watson Test
The Spearman rank - correlation Test.
questions.explanation: The Durbin-Watson test is used for autocorrelation, not heteroskedasticity.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following measures can be effective to control inflation?
options: Salary increment
Reducing bank reserve requirement ratio
Cutting aggregate expenditure
Purchasing bonds from private companies
questions.explanation: Cutting aggregate expenditure can help reduce inflationary pressures.

questions.questionText: Human capital can be described by:
options: Health and education of individual only
Health, education and skill of an individual
Health, education and capital equipment he has
All
questions.explanation: Human capital encompasses health, education, and skills.

questions.questionText: The following are considered in order to estimate shadow wage rate for labor except:
options: Market for unskilled labor is believed to be more competitive than skilled one
Opportunity cost principle
The use of conversion factor
None
questions.explanation: All listed factors are relevant for estimating shadow wage rates.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an assumption of the Lewis two-sector model?
options: Surplus labor in industry.
Positive marginal product of labor in agriculture.
An upward sloping labor supply curve in industry.
None of the above
questions.explanation: The Lewis model assumes surplus labor exists in agriculture, not industry, with an infinitely elastic labor supply to the industrial sector.

questions.questionText: Which issues are needs to be considered while estimating the production and sales of any project?
options: Assume high capacity utilization in the first year of project's foundation
50% - 80% of the project's capacity utilization can be expected within 2 years
It is not necessary to make adjustment for stock in the first year of operation.
All except 'A'
questions.explanation: Adjustments for stock are important in the first year of operation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about the three Keynes demand for money?
options: Transaction demand and precautionary demand related with medium of exchange
Precautionary demand is the demand of money related with wealth portfolio
Both transaction demand and speculative demand held as a medium of exchange
Transaction demand is which rise out of uncertainty.
questions.explanation: Transaction and precautionary demands are both related to the need for money as a medium of exchange.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among main characteristics of diversified farming:
options: Introduction to horticulture, Apiculture and animal husbandry side by side with farming
The success or failure of any efforts to transform traditional agriculture toward diversified one will entirely depend on the farmer's ability and skill
During peak production season human labor is supported by simple agricultural machineries and tools
During slack production season human labor can't be unemployed, instead can engage in off farm income generating activities
questions.explanation: In diversified farming, labor should be able to engage in off-farm income activities during slack seasons, reducing seasonal unemployment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about mixed strategy game?
options: Players assign probability to each strategy
Allows determining Nash equilibrium which do not have Nash equilibrium in pure strategy
Its Nash equilibrium is an equilibrium in which each agent chooses optimal frequency without considering the opponents' frequency
None
questions.explanation: All statements about mixed strategy games are true.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a core requirement for raising agricultural output and productivity in Africa.
options: Pricing policies that reflect the internal market conditions
Introduction of changes in rural institutions that improve production
The introduction of biological, improved water control and chemical innovations
None
questions.explanation: All listed options are core requirements for improving agricultural productivity.

questions.questionText: The main problems of the agriculture sector in Africa is best characterized by:
options: Land defragmentation
Subsistence agriculture and intensive cultivation
Too much land under the control of too few people
All
questions.explanation: All listed issues are significant problems facing the agricultural sector in Africa.

questions.questionText: People could hold some amount of money for the purpose of protection against unexpected transaction in the future. This is:
options: Keynes's liquidity preference theory of transaction motive
Keynes's liquidity preference theory of speculative motive
Keynes's liquidity preference theory of precautionary motive
All of the above
questions.explanation: The precautionary motive refers to holding money for unexpected future transactions.

questions.questionText: If the mean and variance of time series do not vary systematically over time it is called:
options: Stationary
Random
Non-Stationary
Non-Random
questions.explanation: A stationary time series has constant mean and variance over time.

questions.questionText: Which of the following could be used as a test for autocorrelation up to third order?
options: The Durbin Watson test
White's test
The RESET test
The Breusch - Godfrey test
questions.explanation: The Breusch-Godfrey test is used for detecting autocorrelation of higher orders.

questions.questionText: Development economics is concerned with:
options: Efficient allocation of scarce resources
Economic, social and political institutions
Imperfect resource and commodity markets
All of the above
questions.explanation: Development economics encompasses all these aspects.

questions.questionText: The violation of the assumption of constant variance of the residual is known as:
options: Heteroscedasticity
Multicollinearity
Homoscedasticity
Autocorrelation
questions.explanation: Heteroscedasticity occurs when the variance of the residuals is not constant.

questions.questionText: Among the following one shows a region where resources are over-utilized in short-run production period.
options: Over the increasing part of average product curve of a firm
When slope of total product curve reaches maximum point.
When marginal product equals zero
Over the negative part of the slope of total product curve.
questions.explanation: Over-utilization occurs when marginal product is negative.

questions.questionText: Which type of agricultural technology is said to be ill-suited to the physical environment and has the effect of creating more rural unemployment without necessarily lowering per-unit costs of food production?
options: Heavy machineries like airplane sprayer, combine harvester and tractors
Biological innovation like hybrid seeds and biotechnology
Irrigation technologies
Chemical and organic fertilizers, insecticides and pesticides.
questions.explanation: Heavy machinery can lead to unemployment if it replaces labor without increasing efficiency.

questions.questionText: One of the following cannot be an example of financial asset:
options: Share of stock of a company
Building
Bonds
Currency money
questions.explanation: A building is a physical asset, not a financial asset.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not true based on H. Todaro's migration model:
options: Migrant compares actual earning differential between urban formal sector job and rural sector job
Migration is a rational economic decision if long term income differential in favor of urban sector exist even if the current probability of finding a job in urban sector is lower.
The migrant is indifferent between urban sector and rural sector employment if the actual rural sector earning is just equal to expected urban sector earning
The probability of securing urban job is higher if urban unemployment rate is lower.
questions.explanation: In Todaro's model, migration decisions are based on expected urban earnings compared to rural earnings, not actual earnings. Indifference occurs when expected earnings are equal.

questions.questionText: One of the following is the most relevant definition for the word inflation:
options: It is a large rise in general price level in the economy for a fairly long period of time
It is a sudden or unexpected rise in price of basic industrial inputs coupled with considerable fall in aggregate demand
It is a rise in aggregate spending (aggregate demand) of a country
It is an increase in volume of money supply in the economy.
questions.explanation: Inflation is defined as a sustained increase in the general price level.

questions.questionText: Overvaluation of Official exchange rate will create:
options: Imports are cheap to the local citizens
Shortage of foreign exchange rate
Export of the country become expensive to the other world
All
questions.explanation: Overvaluation leads to cheaper imports and expensive exports.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a feature of the history of the agriculture sector in LDCs.
options: The sector has been neglected in the development priorities of governments
The sector accounts for a much lower share of the total output
Productivity in the sector is relatively lower compared to other sectors
None
questions.explanation: All listed features are true regarding the agriculture sector in LDCs.

questions.questionText: A good is fully or potentially tradable if:
options: i.f price > domestic cost of production > f.o.b price
Its domestic cost of production < c.i.f price
Its f.o.b price < its domestic cost of production
Its f.o.b price > its domestic cost of production
questions.explanation: A good is tradable if its f.o.b price exceeds domestic production costs.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following type of migration is becoming an important problem from the standpoint of long-run economic development for the cities of developing countries?
options: Rural – Rural migration
Urban - Rural migration
Rural – Urban migration
Urban - Urban migration
questions.explanation: Rural-urban migration can lead to urban overpopulation and strain on resources.

questions.questionText: One is not an element of the social aspect of the project:
options: The attitude and the likely response of the beneficiary groups
The cultural factors related to the implementation and outcomes of the project
Ecological conditions on site of the project (soil, site hazards, climate etc)
The displacement impact of the project
questions.explanation: Ecological conditions are typically considered environmental rather than social aspects.

questions.questionText: According to the Kuznets hypothesis:
options: Income inequality falls as per capita income rises.
Income inequality first falls then rises as per capita income rises.
Income inequality first rises then falls as per capita income rises.
Income inequality rises as per capita income rises.
questions.explanation: The Kuznets hypothesis suggests that inequality initially increases with development, then decreases.

questions.questionText: Rostow's economic stages are:
options: The traditional society, the preconditions for takeoff, the takeoff, the drive to maturity, and the age of creative destruction.
The traditional society, the preconditions for consumption, the replication, the drive to maturity, and the age of high mass consumption.
The traditional society, the preconditions for takeoff, the takeoff, the drive to maturity, and the age of high mass consumption.
The traditional society, the learning curve, the age of high mass consumption, post-takeoff, and the drive to maturity.
questions.explanation: Rostow's model outlines stages of economic growth leading to high mass consumption.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following does not explain why peasant farmers are risk-averse?
options: Subsistence agriculture is highly risky and uncertain.
The traditional technology and crop patterns known over the years by the farmers have kept them alive.
The goal of peasant subsistent farmer is the maximization of family income.
Peasant farmers have no adequate insurance against imagined or real risks of crop failure.
questions.explanation: The goal of maximizing family income does not inherently lead to risk aversion.

questions.questionText: Identify the one which is not a disadvantage associated with the 'Barter' system (Commodity money):
options: Lacks standardization
Supply uncertainty
Non-portability issue
Low maintenance cost.
questions.explanation: Low maintenance cost is not a disadvantage of the barter system.

questions.questionText: Which one is true according to the accelerator theory of investment?
options: Accelerator theory of investment is the theory of investment that became popular before Keynes.
For the accelerator theory of investment, an increase in income and consumption leads to an increase in investment by multiple amounts.
When investment increases, consumption and income increase by multiple amounts.
The accelerator theory of investment supports the Keynesian theory of investment.
questions.explanation: The accelerator theory posits that increases in income lead to proportionally larger increases in investment.

questions.questionText: From the following statement, one is different from the others by its shapes.
options: Marginal cost
Average total cost
Average fixed cost
Average variable cost.
questions.explanation: Marginal cost typically has a U-shaped curve, while average cost curves (AFC, AVC, ATC) have different shapes. AFC continuously decreases, AVC and ATC are U-shaped but reach their minimum points at different output levels.

questions.questionText: Which one is the first step in financial analysis of the project?
options: Identification of cost and benefit
Preparing cash flow statement of the project
Analysis of profitability of the project
Analysis of risk and uncertainty associated with the project
questions.explanation: Identifying costs and benefits is the foundational step in project financial analysis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a public good?
options: Non-excludability
Non-rivalry
High marginal cost of provision
Free rider problem
questions.explanation: Public goods typically have low marginal costs of provision, not high.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of fiscal policy?
options: To control inflation
To manage the money supply
To influence economic activity through government spending and taxation
To regulate financial institutions
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy aims to influence economic activity through government spending and taxation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a tool of monetary policy?
options: Government spending
Taxation
Open market operations
Public works programs
questions.explanation: Open market operations are a primary tool used in monetary policy to control the money supply.

questions.questionText: What does GDP stand for?
options: Gross Domestic Product
General Domestic Product
Gross Development Product
General Development Product
questions.explanation: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, which measures the total economic output of a country.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a limitation of GDP as an economic indicator?
options: It includes all economic activity
It does not account for income inequality
It measures only formal economic activity
Both B and C
questions.explanation: GDP does not account for income inequality and excludes informal economic activity.

questions.questionText: What is the main goal of economic development?
options: To increase GDP
To improve living standards
To reduce unemployment
To achieve economic growth
questions.explanation: The main goal of economic development is to improve living standards and quality of life.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of a developing economy?
options: High levels of industrialization
Low per capita income
High levels of education
Advanced technological infrastructure
questions.explanation: Developing economies typically have low per capita income and are less industrialized.

questions.questionText: What is the term for the economic situation where demand exceeds supply?
options: Surplus
Shortage
Equilibrium
Deficit
questions.explanation: A shortage occurs when demand exceeds supply.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a consequence of inflation?
options: Increased purchasing power
Decreased cost of living
Uncertainty in the economy
Stability in prices
questions.explanation: Inflation creates uncertainty in the economy as it erodes purchasing power.

questions.questionText: What is the primary function of the World Bank?
options: To provide military aid
To promote international trade
To provide financial and technical assistance to developing countries
To regulate global financial markets
questions.explanation: The World Bank provides financial and technical assistance to developing countries for development projects.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a method of measuring economic growth?
options: Consumer Price Index
Gross Domestic Product
Unemployment Rate
Balance of Trade
questions.explanation: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is a primary method for measuring economic growth.

questions.questionText: What is the term for the economic policy that aims to reduce government spending and increase taxes?
options: Expansionary fiscal policy
Contractionary fiscal policy
Monetary policy
Supply-side policy
questions.explanation: Contractionary fiscal policy aims to reduce government spending and increase taxes to control inflation.
